questions.question: Which of the following Harappan sites do not have evidence of fortification?
questions.solution:
__**Chanhudaro**__ does not have evidence of fortification. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• Chanhudaro is the **only** major Indus Valley Civilization (IVC) city that does not have a fortified citadel. 
 
• The citadel was a fortified area that was typically located in the **highest part of the city** and was used as a **place of refuge during times of attack. **
 
• The absence of a citadel at Chanhudaro suggests that the city was not as concerned about security as other IVC cities.
 
• There are a few possible explanations for why Chanhudaro did not have a citadel. 
 
• One possibility is that the city was located in a relatively safe area and was not at risk of attack. 
 
• Another possibility is that the city was not as important as other IVC cities and did not need the same level of security. 
 
• Finally, it is also possible that the city was **simply not wealthy enough to afford to build a citadel.**
 
• Whatever the reason, the absence of a citadel at Chanhudaro is a unique feature of this IVC city. 
 
• It provides us with some clues about the nature of this ancient civilization and the different ways in which IVC cities were organized.
 
• Here are some other interesting facts about Chanhudaro:
 
 
• **​It is located in the Larkana district of Sindh, Pakistan.**
 
• **It was excavated by N.G. Majumdar in 1931.**
 
• **It is a small city, covering an area of only 7 hectares.**
 
• **It is famous for its production of carnelian beads.**
 
• **It also had a number of other industries, including shell-cutting, metal-working, and seal-making.**
 
• **The city was abandoned around 1700 BCE.**
 
 
 
• The lack of a citadel at Chanhudaro is just one of the many mysteries that surround this ancient city. 
 
• However, it is a mystery that continues to fascinate archaeologists and historians.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **​Bhirrana:**__

 __
 
• **​**__The oldest known Harappan site dates back to the 8th-7th millennium BCE. 
 
• It is located on the left bank of the Ghaggar river in Haryana, India.
 
• Bhirrana is notable for its well-preserved architecture, including houses, streets, and drainage systems.
 
• It has also yielded a number of artefacts, including seals, figurines, and pottery.
 
 
 
• __**Rakhigarhi:**__
 __
 
• **​**__The largest known Harappan site, covering an area of over 350 hectares. 
 
• It is located in the same area as Bhirrana and is thought to have been the capital of the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• Rakhigarhi is still under excavation, but it is already clear that it was a major urban centre.
 
• The site has revealed evidence of a complex society with a stratified social hierarchy.
 
 
 
• __**Banawali:**__ 
 
 
• ​A medium-sized Harappan site, covering an area of about 100 hectares. 
 
• It is located in the Hisar district of Haryana, India.
 
• Banawali is also a well-preserved site, and it has yielded a number of important artefacts, including a bronze chariot and a seal with a unicorn motif.

questions.question: The site of Harappa is located on the bank of river
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ravi.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Ravi:**

 
• It is **one of the five tributaries of the Indus River that give the Punjab** (meaning “Five Rivers”) its name.** Other tributaries are: Jhelum, Chenab, Beas and Sutlej.**
 
• Transboundary River: **It rises in the Himalayas in Himachal Pradesh (India**) and **flows to the Pakistani border** and along it for more than 80 km before entering Pakistan’s Punjab province.
 
• Harappa is an **archaeological site in Punjab, Pakistan, about 24 km west of Sahiwal**.
 
• The **Bronze Age Harappan civilisation, now more often called the Indus Valley Civilisation**, is **named after the site**, which **takes its name from a modern village** near the **former course of the Ravi River**, which now runs 8 km to the north.

**Harappa:**

 
• The site of the ancient city contains the **ruins of a Bronze Age fortified city**, which was part of the Harappan civilisation centred in Sindh and the Punjab.
 
• The city is believed to have had as many as **23,500 residents and occupied about 150 hectares (370 acres) with clay brick houses **at its greatest **extent during the Mature Harappan phase (2600 BC – 1900 BC)**, which is considered large for its time.
 
• Per the archaeological convention of naming a **previously unknown civilisation by its first excavated site, the Indus Valley Civilisation is also called the Harappan Civilisation.**
 
• The ancient city of Harappa was **heavily damaged under British and French rule**, when bricks from the ruins were used as track ballast in the construction of the **Lahore–Multan Railway.**

questions.question: Who composed the Vedas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aryans.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vedas**:

 
 
• A **vast collection of religious writings with ancient Indian origins** is known as the Vedas.
 
• **Written in Vedic Sanskrit**, the books are the oldest body of Sanskrit literature and the earliest Hindu scriptures.
 
• The** Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda, and Atharvaveda are the four Vedas.**
 
• Rig Veda **composers describe themselves as Aryans.**
 
• Each Veda is divided into four sections:
 
 
• The Samhitas, which contain mantras and benedictions
 
• The Brahmanas, which explain and comment on rituals, ceremonies, and sacrifices (Yajnas)
 
• The Aranyakas, which contain texts on these topics
 
• The Upanishads, which contain texts on philosophy, meditation, and spiritual knowledge.

questions.question: What was the capital of Vajji Mahajanapada?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vaishali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Vajji, also known as Vrijji or Vriji, was an important and powerful confederacy in ancient India. It was one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas (great kingdoms) mentioned in ancient Buddhist and Jain texts.
 
• **Location:** 
 
 
• The exact geographical contours of the Vajji confederacy are not recorded in history.
 
• However, it is believed to be located north of the Ganges in Bihar and likely extended to the Madhesh region of Nepal.
 
• The capital city of this confederation was Vaishali, which is identified with the present village of Basarh in the Vaishali district of Bihar, India.
 
 
 
• **Government:** 
 
 
• The governance of Vajji was unique compared to the other kingdoms of the era.

questions.question: Which animal was not known to the Indus people?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Lion.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indus Valley Civilization, also known as the Harappan Civilization, was one of the world's earliest urban civilizations, located in the northwestern region of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The people of this civilization were known for their advanced urban planning, sophisticated craftsmanship, and strong organizational skills.
 
• They domesticated and used various animals for different purposes. These animals included sheep, goat, humped and humpless bull, buffalo, boar, dog, cat, pig, fowl, deer, tortoise, elephants, camel, rhinoceros, and tiger.
 
• However, there is no archaeological evidence to suggest that the people of the Indus Valley Civilization were familiar with the lion. This could be due to various reasons such as the lion not being native to the areas where this civilization flourished, or the lion not being a significant part of their culture or economy.

**Therefore, based on current archaeological findings and historical records, it is accurate to say that the lion was not known to the people of the Indus Valley Civilization.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Important Features of Indus Valley Civilization**.

 
 
• ​The grid system of town Planning.
 
• Citadel ( for administrative and religious purposes) and lower town ( residence of common people).
 
• large-scale use of burnt bricks and the absence of stone buildings.
 
• Houses had many rooms with a square courtyard, private wells, kitchens, and bathing space.
 
• Well laid out underground drainage system.

questions.question: The Rig Veda is a collection of ________ hymns.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Rig Veda **consists of a total of **1,028 hymns,** divided into **ten books** known as** Mandalas.**
 
• Each **Mandala** is further divided into **hymns, **which are composed in various poetic meters.
 
• **The hymns** are attributed to differen**t seers or rishis**, who were the ancient sages or poets believed to have received divine revelations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Vedas are a collection of **ancient Hindu scriptures** and are considered the **oldest **and most authoritative texts in Hinduism.
 
• There are four main Vedas: **the Rig Veda, the Sama Veda, the Yajur Veda, and the Atharva Veda**. Each Veda has its own unique characteristics and content.
 
• **Rig Veda:** It contains a collection of 1,028 hymns, or sukta, composed in Vedic Sanskrit. 
 
• **Sama Veda**: The Sama Veda consists of a collection of melodies or chants derived from the hymns of the Rig Veda.
 
 
• The Sama Veda focuses on the musical aspects of the hymns and is often considered a guidebook for priests involved in chanting and singing during rituals.
 
 
 
• **Yajur Veda:** The Yajur Veda is primarily a guidebook for priests involved in performing sacrificial rituals.
 
 
• The former contains the prose formulas along with some hymns, while the latter contains the prose formulas embedded within the hymns.
 
 
 
• **Atharva Veda:** The Atharva Veda is distinct from the other three Vedas as it focuses more on practical aspects of life and includes hymns related to healing, magic, charms, and rituals for protection against evil spirits and diseases.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of Mahajanapadas from west to east?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Avanti, Chedi, Vatsa, Magadha, ____Anga__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• **Avanti **was one of the most powerful Mahajanapadas in the 6th century B.C.

 
 
• The core area of this kingdom would roughly correspond to the** Ujjain district of Madhya Pradesh**, extending up to the river Narmada.
 
 
 
• **The Chedi** territory roughly corresponds to the eastern parts of the modern **Bundelkhand**.
 
 
• It might have stretched up to the **Malwa plateau.** Sisupala the famous enemy of Krishna, was a Chedi ruler. 
 
 
 
• **Vatsa **with its capital at Kausambi was one of the most powerful principalities of the sixth century B.C.
 
 
• Kausambi has been identified with modem Kosam or the river Yamuna near** ****Prayagraj. **
 
 
 
• **Magadha** consisted of the areas around Patna and Gaya in south Bihar.
 
 
• It was protected by the rivers Son and Ganga on its north and west.
 
• Towards the south, it reached up to the **Chotanagpur plateau.**
 
• In the east the river Champa separated it from Anga.
 
• Its capital was called **Girivraja or Rajagriha.**
 
 
 
• **Anga** comprised the districts of Bhagalpur and Monghyr in Bihar.
 
 
• It may have extended northwards to the **river Kosi and included some parts of the district of Purnea.**
 
• It was located to the east of Magadha and west of the Rajamahal hills. 
 
 

**Hence, option 3 is the correct answer**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/04460ee5c8baeb44d25eb74c1daa2d1748a8057301e4cf8627b57063daf38dfa.png]
